survey: A red British telephone box stands upright on a dark grey plinth on a flat green floor, seen in three-quarter view from slightly above eye level. The door face, which holds the handle, turns toward the viewer on the right. The left side face turns away and is drawn narrower, and its glazing bars are compressed to match. The top of the plinth is visible, which agrees with the slightly high camera. The plinth sits flat on the floor. The domed roof sits square on the box, with a crown badge and a sign panel on each face, and each sign follows the angle of its own face. The box's verticals stay vertical and parallel. Each window grid's rows run parallel to the top and bottom edges of its face. The pay phone is mounted on the back wall and seen through the door glass; its keypad faces the viewer, as it should for a wall-mounted unit behind the door. All parts agree on one camera.
